content.title: About
content.content: Brewed coffee made from ground beans (Coffea arabica or C. robusta) is a popular beverage containing caffeine, aromatic compounds, and antioxidants. Brewing releases its characteristic aroma, a slightly bitter taste, and a stimulating effect.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Coffee is the second most consumed drink in the world after water.
The first documented method of brewing coffee appeared in the 15th century in Yemen.
There are over 100 coffee varieties, but more than 60 % of global production comes from Arabica.
Caffeine in coffee stimulates the central nervous system, enhancing alertness.
Coffee can be prepared in many ways: espresso, drip, French press, Turkish, and more.

items.title: Boosts alertness
items.content: Caffeine raises adrenaline levels, improving concentration and reaction time.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Coffee is high in polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports metabolism
items.content: Caffeine may increase metabolic rate and aid fat burning.

items.title: May lower risk of certain diseases
items.content: Moderate coffee consumption is linked to reduced risk of Parkinson’s disease, type‑2 diabetes, and some cancers.

items.title: Improves mood
items.content: Caffeine stimulates dopamine and serotonin production, which can lift mood.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat after coffee.

items.title: Blood pressure increase
items.content: High doses of caffeine can temporarily raise blood pressure, important for hypertensive persons.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Coffee can irritate the stomach and cause heartburn in people with high gastric acidity.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Caffeine may amplify the effects of certain medications, such as CNS stimulants.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Coffee is usually served hot, but it can be cooled and made into iced coffee. Milk, cream, sugar, syrups, or spices are added to taste. For a milder flavor, use a coarser grind and shorter brew time.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ground coffee in an airtight container in a cool, dark place, preferably in the refrigerator, to preserve aroma. Avoid prolonged exposure to air, moisture, and light, as they accelerate oxidation.
